name: Julie Bess Aimen
evaluation: Judge Aimen was admitted to the Illinois bar in 1984. Prior to her election in 2020 she was a sole practitioner with concentrations in criminal defense, family and civil rights matters and appellate law. After the initial assignment, since 2022 she has been assigned to Domestic Relations Division at the 1st Municipal District (Daley Center). She has been a committee member for several bar associations and was on the Board of Directors for the Chicago Council of Lawyers. Attorneys consider her to be smart, hardworking, professional, and patient with the many pro se litigants who appear before her.

name: Regina Ann Mescall
evaluation: Judge Mescall was admitted to the Illinois bar in 2007 and elected to the Cook Circuit Court in 2020; this is her first retention election. Judge Mescall has been assigned to Domestic Relations in Fifth Municipal District (Bridgeview) since July 2025. Before this, she sat in the First Municipal District – Civil Jury. Before becoming a judge, she was a prosecutor in New Mexico from 2002 until 2007 when she moved to Chicago and became an Assistant State’s Attorney in the Felony Trial Division. Judge Mescall is a member of several bar associations and teaches Trial Advocacy at the University of Illinois Law School. Comments about her temperament, sensitivity and preparedness were uniformly positive. There were concerns voiced about her legal knowledge and impartiality in her new assignment in Domestic Relations Court. She appears interested in improving and willing to learn.

name: Teresa Molina - Gonzalez
evaluation: Judge Molina-Gonzalez was admitted to the Illinois bar in 2001. Prior to her appointment to the circuit court in 2019, she was a Cook County Assistant State’s Attorney in the Child Support Enforcement Division and the Felony Trial Division; and Chief of Real Estate Prosecutions for the Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation. She was elected to a countywide vacancy in 2020 and is assigned to the Fourth Municipal District (Maywood) where her duties rotate every 4 months. She has covered various courtrooms, including misdemeanors, preliminary hearings, domestic violence, and occasionally felony and mental health courts. Judge Molina-Gonzalez has a variety of community engagements, including work with Special Olympics, Friendship Animal Protective League, Corazon Community Services, and the Arts Alliance of Forest Park, to name only a few. Attorneys report that she is knowledgeable and research cases; is level-headed and respectful.

name: Thomas J. Byrne
evaluation: Judge Byrne was admitted to the Illinois bar in 1989. After a career as a prosecutor, he was elected to a circuit court countywide vacancy in 2008; retained in 2014 and 2020. He has been assigned to the Leighton Criminal Courthouse since 2013, presiding over felony cases. He has been a speaker on legal issues, a mock trial volunteer, and a mentor judge, and is a member of various bar and judicial organizations., Attorneys praised his fairness and demeanor and reported that he is respected by both sides as a judge who follows the law.

name: John Michael Allegretti
evaluation: Judge Allegretti was admitted to the Illinois bar in 1995. He was appointed to the circuit court in May 2014; elected in November 2014; retained in 2020. He is currently assigned to the First Municipal District, presiding over civil non-jury trials; previous assignments include the County Division, First Municipal and Traffic. He has spoken and written on legal issues, is a member and has served on committees for various bar associations and has served as a volunteer mentor for new judges. Prior to his appointment he was general counsel for the Cook County Treasurer’s office. Attorneys praised his legal knowledge, research skills, professionalism and fairness.

name: Tyria B. Walton
evaluation: Judge Walton was admitted to the Illinois bar in 1997. She briefly had her own practice before joining the Office of the Cook County Public Defender, where she was assigned to the Markham courthouse as a trial attorney. Since her appointment to the circuit court in 2019, she served in the First Municipal District, and the Maywood Courthouse. She was elected in 2020 and presently hears felony cases at both bench and jury trials at the Leighton Criminal Courthouse. Judge Walton has been active as a speaker for both legal (AOIC) and community (local churches and Kennedy-King College) events. She is an officer of the Illinois Judicial Council. She has also been active with the local branch of the NAACP. References uniformly praised her Legal knowledge, temperament, character, and professionalism.

name: Patricia M. Fallon
evaluation: Judge Fallon was admitted to the Illinois bar in 2001. She was appointed to the circuit court in 2019 and elected in 2020. She has been assigned to Domestic Relations since July 2023, after initial assignments in Traffic and First Municipal. Prior to her appointment she was Chief of Human Resources for the Cook County Recorder of Deeds; she had been a prosecutor prior to taking that position. She has been a speaker in legal matters, a moot court judge, and a committee member for the Illinois State Bar Association. Attorneys reported that she demonstrates strong legal knowledge and analytical ability and is well-respected for her preparedness and fairness.

name: Kristal Rivers
evaluation: Judge Rivers was admitted to the Illinois bar in 1996 and the Texas bar in 1996. She was appointed to the circuit court in June 2014; elected to a countywide vacancy in 2014 and retained in 2020. From May 2015 until October 2021, she served in the Juvenile Justice Division. In 2021 she was assigned to the Misdemeanor Petty and Domestic Violence Room in Bridgeview, where she currently hears criminal bench and jury trials. Judge Rivers is said to be knowledgeable, and able to make fair and thoughtful rulings. She is sensitive to issues confronting the diverse population that appears before her. She is respectful, calm, consistent, and predictable. Judge Rivers is ‘always on time’ and prepared.

name: Lorraine Mary Murphy
evaluation: Judge Murphy was admitted to the Illinois bar in 2003. Prior to her election to a countywide vacancy in 2020, she was a career Assistant State’s Attorney assigned to the Leighton Criminal Courthouse in the Appeals Division and at the Sixth Municipal District (Markham). Since March of 2024, Judge Murphy has been assigned to a felony courtroom in the Second Municipal District (Skokie); she served as a floater in Skokie from October 2021 until her present assignment. Prior to that, she was briefly assigned to Room 1104 in the Daley Center and to Traffic Court. Judge Murphy reports she has worked with the Outreach Community Center in Little Village. She has participated in their school and summer programs, including chaperoning field trips to various museums. Reports indicate that Judge Murphy has a good knowledge of criminal law and procedures. However, concerns were expressed about her lack of impartiality in criminal cases in favor of the prosecution and what the Committee felt was careless preparation of her judicial evaluation questionnaire.

name: Laura Ayala - Gonzalez
evaluation: Judge Ayala-Gonzalez was admitted to the Illinois bar in 2003. She was elected to the circuit court in 2020; since December 2022, she has been assigned to the Leighton Criminal Courthouse where she presides over a felony call. Prior to this she had been assigned to First Municipal and Traffic. She serves as secretary for the Illinois Latino Judges Association, is a committee member for the Illinois Judges Association, and is a member of various other bar associations. She has been a speaker on legal topics to students, a mock trial volunteer, and is on the Board of Trinity High School. Attorneys and judges praised her legal knowledge and ability, describing her as one of the stronger jurists in the Criminal Division. She is considered to be fair, effective, diligent, and prepared.

name: Levander Smith, Jr.
evaluation: Judge Smith was admitted to the Illinois bar in 1993, and the Missouri bar in 1999. He was appointed to the circuit court in March 2019; appointed as an Associate Judge in January 2020 serving briefly in Traffic Court and Domestic Violence Court. After his election to a countywide vacancy in 2020, he has been assigned to the Child Protection Division of Juvenile Court, where he conducts bench trials and hearings. He also volunteers twice a month for ‘benchmark hearings’, which are proactive meetings with youth (16 - 20) in foster care who are focused on transitioning them to independence as they become adults. Prior to taking the bench, Judge Smith’s legal career focused on family and child protection issues. He is a member of several bar associations, has volunteered in the community and has received awards for his judicial service.

name: Bridget Anne Mitchell
evaluation: Judge Mitchell was admitted to the Illinois bar in 1981. After a career as a civil litigator, she was elected in 2014 and retained in 2020. Her first assignment was in the Traffic Division, then to the Foreclosure Section of the Chancery Division. Since 2017 she has been assigned to jury trials in the Law Division where she handles all aspects of litigation. She has served on committees for several bar associations, including the Illinois State Bar Association and the Chicago Bar Association, is a member of several judicial associations, and has been a speaker on legal topics. Judge Mitchell is noted to have excellent legal knowledge, to treat everyone equally, and to be impartial with high integrity. Judge Mitchell is described as having great demeanor, being calm and respectful. She is punctual and diligent, investing adequate time for all cases, though some attorneys thought she moved cases too slowly.

name: Pamela Reaves - Harris
evaluation: Judge Reaves-Harris was admitted to the Illinois bar in 1992 and elected in 2020. She started her judicial career in Traffic Court, where she served until her current assignment in November 2021 to Housing Court. Her duties include dealing with all municipal housing code violations, for all structural including residential, commercial, industrial, and institutional. Before becoming a judge, she served as an Administrative Law Judge for various municipalities, including Chicago, and served as a State Representative for the 10 District from January 2015 to January 2017. From 2017 to November 2020, she was Special Assistant to Legal Affairs in Cook County Government. Judge Reaves-Harris was praised for her legal knowledge, sensitivity, character, diligence, and temperament.

name: Joan E. Powell
evaluation: Judge Powell was admitted to the Illinois bar in 1992. She worked for the Cook County State’s Attorney’s Office, Civil Division, and in private solo practice for 14 years before being elected to the circuit court in 2000. She has been assigned to the Law Division since 2014, where she hears jury and occasionally bench trials, along with necessary motions. Lawyers and judges praised Judge Powell in all areas being evaluated. Her legal knowledge, sensitivity to diversity, professionalism, impartiality, and temperament were excellent. She is described as hard working, diligent, and punctual.

name: Christ Stacey
evaluation: Judge Stacey was admitted to practice in 1982. In 1992 and up until his election, he had his own solo firm, concentrating in tort and commercial litigation in both state and federal courts. Judge Stacey was elected to the circuit court in 2020; he served briefly in the Traffic Division. From January 2021 until December 2021, Judge Stacey was assigned to Evictions Court, where he presented over motions, bench trials and settlement conference. Since December 2021, he has been assigned Civil Jury Room where he hears bench and jury trials in addition to motions and settlement conferences. Judge Stacey is a member of the Chicago Lincoln Inn of Court, leading and attending pupilage sessions. He is also involved in ‘hands on’ work with World Relief International.
